sources_read.section: §1 ownership table; §4 import rules; §5.6 internal/auth; §6 Transport/middleware; §7.9 DB pool sizing
current_profile_id(), teams/team_members/team_role, is_team_member(), is_team_leader(), sessions/board_columns/boards chain, can_access_session()

scope: Implement the real internal/auth package per §5.6: JWKS-based Supabase JWT verification, and an authorizer that is an exact Go mirror of the schema's SQL security-definer helpers (current_profile_id, is_team_member, is_team_leader, can_access_session), plus a TTL cache and the two Gin middleware files from §6 that use them. Wire one protected example route (GET /v1/me) to prove the chain works end to end. Does NOT include: RLS policy changes, new business endpoints beyond /v1/me, membership-cache invalidation on role change (§5.6 mentions 'invalidated on role change' — implemented as TTL expiry only, no realtime/pubsub invalidation hook, since no such wiring exists anywhere yet), or a docker-based integration test against real Postgres (no testcontainers/Docker available in this session — unit tests use fakes instead, flagged in test.json).

acceptance_criteria.text: kernel.AuthUserID/ProfileID/TeamID/SessionID are distinct string(uuid) types, not raw strings, so a caller can't pass the wrong id type where the compiler could catch it.

postgres.NewPool(ctx, cfg) applies §7.9's required pgx settings (DefaultQueryExecMode=Exec, StatementCacheCapacity=0) unconditionally, since the transaction pooler breaks server-side prepared statements even in local dev against port 54322 direct connect — same code path either way, no special-case for direct vs. pooled.
jwt.Verifier fetches {SupabaseURL}/auth/v1/.well-known/jwks.json, caches keys by kid, refetches once on an unknown kid (key rotation), and rejects expired/malformed/wrong-issuer tokens.

Authorizer methods take a DB interface (satisfied by *pgxpool.Pool) so they're unit-testable with a fake, and their SQL matches the schema function bodies field-for-field (team_members.team_id/profile_id/role; sessions->board_columns->boards join for can_access_session).
CachedAuthorizer wraps Authorizer, TTL default 60s (matches §5.6's '<=60s'), keyed per (profile,team) and per (profile,session).

middleware.Auth() populates gin context with kernel.ProfileID from a verified Bearer token (401 on missing/invalid); middleware.RequireTeamMember()/RequireSessionAccess() read a URL param and 403 on failure, 500 mapped via shared/errs on unexpected DB error.
GET /v1/me (behind Auth()) returns the resolved profile id; go test ./... covers jwt verify (real RSA keypair + httptest JWKS server), authorizer logic (fake DB), and cache TTL expiry.

open_questions: current_profile_id() resolves via profile_identities keyed on auth_user_id = auth.uid() — this task's ResolveProfileID does the same lookup in Go (profile_identities WHERE auth_user_id = $1). If a signed-in auth user has no profile_identities row yet (e.g. the 0002_auth_trigger.sql bridge hasn't fired), ResolveProfileID returns 'not found' as a 403, not a 500 — flagging this as a judgment call, not silently assumed correct.

Supabase local/default projects issue HS256 JWTs signed with a shared secret unless 'asymmetric JWT' / JWKS is explicitly enabled on the project. 03-backend-folder-architecture.md §5.6 says 'verify via JWKS' without qualification, so this task implements JWKS (RS256/ES256) verification only, matching the doc literally. If the actual Supabase project this connects to uses the legacy HS256 shared-secret model instead, jwt.go will need an HS256 fallback path — that's a real risk worth confirming against the live project before this ships past local testing.

No Docker/testcontainers available in this session, so §8's 'Integration | test/integration/ | testcontainers Postgres + real migrations' row is not exercised for this task — authorizer SQL is verified by inspection against thinkboard-schema-final.sql plus unit tests against a fake DB, not a real one.
risks: If the target Supabase project uses HS256 (legacy JWT secret) instead of JWKS, every request will 401 until jwt.go gets an HS256 path — this is the single biggest correctness risk of this task and should be checked against the real project's Auth settings before relying on this in an environment beyond local dev.
membership cache has no invalidation hook (TTL-only) — a role change (e.g. demoting a leader) can be honored up to 60s late. Acceptable per the doc's own '<=60s' framing but worth restating.
